about.ex: The trip takes about two hours.

according.ex: According to the report, prices rose again.

achieved.ex: The team achieved its sales target in May.

acknowledged.ex: He acknowledged that the plan had problems.

acquired.ex: The bank acquired a small rival last year.

across.es: en todo; a lo largo de

act.en: do something to deal with a problem
act.ex: We must act before it is too late.

added.ex: She added sugar to her tea.

administration.en: when experts run a company that cannot pay debts
administration.ex: The airline went into administration last spring.
administration.ja: 経営破綻による管財手続き

example.en: The airline went into administration after months of losses.
example.zh: 該航空公司在虧損數月後進入破產管理程序。

note.meaning: 破產管理；公司無力償債時由外部專家接管。
note.usage: 常用 go into / enter administration；與 liquidation（清算）不同，目標是挽救公司。

noteEn.meaning: when outside experts run a company that cannot pay its debts.

noteEs.exampleTr: La aerolínea entró en administración tras meses de pérdidas.
noteEs.meaning: proceso en que expertos externos gestionan una empresa insolvente.
noteEs.usage: Se usa go into / enter administration; busca salvar la empresa.

noteHi.exampleTr: महीनों के घाटे के बाद एयरलाइन प्रशासन में चली गई।
noteHi.meaning: ऐसी प्रक्रिया जिसमें दिवालिया कंपनी को बाहरी विशेषज्ञ चलाते हैं।
noteHi.usage: go into / enter administration के रूप में प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その航空会社は数か月の赤字の後、管財手続きに入った。
noteJa.meaning: 支払い不能の会社を外部の専門家が管理する手続き。
noteJa.usage: go into / enter administration の形で使う。清算とは異なる。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 항공사는 몇 달간의 적자 끝에 법정관리에 들어갔다.
noteKo.meaning: 지급 불능 회사를 외부 전문가가 관리하는 절차.
noteKo.usage: go into / enter administration 형태로 쓴다. 청산과 다르다.

administrators.en: experts who run a failed company
administrators.ex: The administrators hope to sell the shops.

adversely.ex: Crops were adversely affected by drought.

affected.ex: Flights were affected by the strong winds.

afloat.ex: The small shop struggled to stay afloat.

alarmed.ex: The sudden price rise alarmed shoppers.

alixpartners.ja: アリックスパートナーズ

already.ex: The tickets are already sold out.

also.ex: She speaks French and also some Spanish.

alternative.ex: We found an alternative route home.

amounting.ex: Her debts amount to over five thousand euro.

announcement.ex: The airline made an announcement about the delay.

any.en: one or some, of whatever kind

appointed.en: chose someone officially for a job
appointed.ex: The board appointed a new manager last week.

approximately.en: close to a number, not exact
approximately.ex: The trip takes approximately three hours.

are.en: to exist; to have a quality
are.ex: There are three parks near my home.

arm.en: a part or branch of a big company
arm.ex: The bank's insurance arm made a profit.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the party.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

asked.ex: We asked the guide for directions.

at.en: in a place, time or level

balance.es: en el aire (hang in the balance)
balance.ex: The team's future hangs in the balance.
balance.zh: 懸而未決（hang in the balance）

banner.ex: The shops trade under a new banner.
banner.zh: 品牌；名號（under the banner：以…名號）

been.ex: She has been a teacher for ten years.

before.ex: I had never seen snow before.

best.ex: This is the best pizza in town.

between.en: in the space or time separating two things

bid.ex: In a bid to save money, they closed early.
bid.zh: 企圖；努力（in a bid to：為了）

bought.en: paid money to get (past of buy)

brothers.en: part of the firm name Gordon Brothers

brought.en: asked someone to come and help
brought.ex: The council brought in experts to help.

budget.ex: We flew with a budget airline.

business.en: the work of buying, selling or producing
business.ex: The bakery has been in business for fifty years.

called.ex: Critics called the decision a mistake.

carry.ex: Please carry on with your work.

certainty.en: being sure about what will happen
certainty.ex: Investors want certainty before they spend money.

chain.en: a group of shops with one owner
chain.ex: The coffee chain opened ten new cafés.

chains.en: groups of shops with one owner
chains.ex: Big chains often pay lower prices to suppliers.

cheap.ex: These shoes were cheap but comfortable.

closely.ex: Doctors are watching the patient closely.

collaborate.ex: The two universities collaborate on research.

collapsed.ex: The travel firm collapsed with large debts.

company.ex: The company employs two hundred people.

competition.en: trying to win customers from others
competition.ex: Competition between airlines keeps fares low.

compounded.ex: The flood damage was compounded by heavy winds.

example.en: Bad weather compounded the traffic problems.
example.zh: 惡劣天氣使交通問題雪上加霜。

note.usage: 多用被動 be compounded by；受詞通常是 problem、difficulty 等負面名詞。

noteEn.meaning: To make a bad problem even worse.

noteEs.exampleTr: El mal tiempo agravó los problemas de tráfico.
noteEs.usage: Muy común en pasiva be compounded by; con problem, difficulty, etc.

noteHi.exampleTr: खराब मौसम ने यातायात की समस्याओं को और बढ़ा दिया।
noteHi.meaning: (क्रिया) समस्या को और बढ़ाना या बदतर बनाना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर कर्मवाच्य be compounded by; problem, difficulty जैसे शब्दों के साथ।

noteJa.exampleTr: 悪天候が交通問題をさらに悪化させた。
noteJa.meaning: （動詞）問題をさらに悪化させる。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be compounded by が多く、problem や difficulty など否定的な語と使う。

noteKo.usage: 수동태 be compounded by가 흔하며 problem, difficulty 같은 부정적 명사와 쓴다.

conceded.en: admitted that something is true, often unwillingly
conceded.ex: He conceded that the test was too hard.

concern.ex: The main questions concern cost and timing.

consequently.ex: The road was closed; consequently, buses were late.

considerable.ex: The project will need considerable investment.

contact.ex: Call the contact centre for help.

control.en: the power to limit or manage something
control.ex: The town has strict control of parking.

cost.ex: The cost of food keeps rising.

costs.en: amounts of money needed for things
costs.ex: Care costs are a big worry for families.

dealz.en: a cheap shop chain in Ireland

decline.en: a fall in number or quality
decline.ex: There has been a decline in wild birds.

delay.en: a time when something happens later
delay.ex: There was a short delay before take-off.

delivered.ex: The team delivered big savings this year.

difficulties.ex: Many families have difficulty paying rent.

discount.en: money taken off the normal price
discount.ex: Students get a ten percent discount.

discounter.en: a company that sells goods cheaply
discounter.ex: The discounter opened a store in Galway.

discounters.ex: Discounters have won many new customers.

do.ex: Do you want to join us?

elements.ex: The plan has three key elements.

emphasised.en: said something strongly to show importance
emphasised.ex: She emphasised the need for safety.

employees.en: people who work for a company
employees.ex: The firm has two hundred employees.

employment.ex: Employment in the region is rising.

engage.ex: Councils must engage with local residents.

engagement.ex: The union called for engagement with management.

entered.ex: Thousands entered the country last year.

enterprise.en: business; used in the ministry's name
enterprise.ex: The Minister for Enterprise spoke at the conference.

erosion.en: slow loss or weakening over time
erosion.ex: The erosion of trust is hard to fix.

example.en: Rising costs caused a steady erosion of profits.
example.zh: 成本上升使利潤持續流失。

note.usage: 比喻用法：erosion of + 名詞（trust, sales, margins, rights）。

noteEn.meaning: slow reduction or weakening of something.

noteEs.exampleTr: El aumento de costes provocó una erosión constante de los beneficios.
noteEs.usage: Uso figurado: erosion of trust / margins.

noteHi.exampleTr: बढ़ती लागत से मुनाफ़ा लगातार घटता गया।
noteHi.meaning: धीरे-धीरे कम होना या कमज़ोर होना।
noteHi.usage: erosion of trust / margins जैसे प्रयोग।

noteJa.exampleTr: コスト上昇で利益が徐々に目減りした。
noteJa.usage: 比喩的に erosion of trust / margins と使う。

noteKo.usage: 비유적으로 erosion of trust / margins 형태로 쓴다.

evaluated.en: judged the value or effect of
evaluated.ex: The plan was evaluated by experts.

experts.ex: Experts warn the river may rise further.

explores.ex: The report explores ways to cut costs.

exposed.en: likely to be hurt by something
exposed.ex: Small farms are exposed to price changes.

face.ex: The plan may face strong opposition.
face.ja: 直面する；（in the face of：〜に直面して）
face.zh: 面臨；（in the face of：面對）

fall.ex: House prices may fall next year.

far.ex: The problem is far from solved.

finance.en: money matters managed by a government
finance.zh: 財政（Minister for Finance：財政部長）

find.ex: You will find out your gate at the airport.

firm.ex: She works for a law firm.

floundering.en: struggling badly and close to failing
floundering.ex: The floundering shop closed in March.

former.en: having been something in the past
former.ex: The former mayor opened the new park.

forward.ex: We need a clear way forward.

further.ex: A further ten jobs will be created.

féin's.en: belonging to the Sinn Féin party

ged.en: first name of politician Ged Nash

generated.ex: The plan generated a lot of anger.

gone.ex: The free bags offer is now gone.

gordon.en: part of the firm name Gordon Brothers

government.en: the group that runs a country
government.ex: The government plans to build more homes.

group.en: a number of people or things together
group.ex: A group of students visited the museum.

had.ex: The council had already made its decision.

hanging.ex: The deal is hanging in the balance.
hanging.zh: 懸而未決（hang in the balance）

harder.ex: The rain made the walk harder.

has.en: used to form the present perfect
has.ex: The town has a long history.

have.ex: We have to leave early tomorrow.
have.ja: 持つ（have to：〜しなければならない）

heading.ex: They were heading home after work.

help.ex: The money will help pay for new schools.

high.ex: The stakes are high for small farmers.

house.en: a company of a certain type
house.ex: She works for a big publishing house.
house.zh: 公司；機構（investment house：投資公司）

however.ex: The plan is cheap; however, it is slow.

hurt.ex: Nobody was hurt in the accident.

immediately.ex: Please call me immediately when you arrive.

increase.ex: There was a 10% increase in sales.

indeed.en: used to add a stronger point
indeed.ex: Prices rose sharply; indeed, rent doubled.

indicated.ex: The minister indicated she would support it.

inflation.ex: High inflation makes food more expensive.

is.en: to exist; to have a quality
is.ex: The shop is on the main street.

january.en: the first month of the year

example.en: Late payments could jeopardise the whole project.
example.zh: 延遲付款可能危及整個計畫。

note.usage: jeopardise + 名詞（jobs, safety, future）；英式拼法 -ise，美式 -ize。

noteEn.meaning: putting something in danger of being lost or harmed.
noteEn.usage: Often used with jobs, safety or someone's future.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los pagos tardíos podrían poner en peligro todo el proyecto.

noteHi.exampleTr: देर से भुगतान पूरी परियोजना को खतरे में डाल सकता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 支払いの遅れはプロジェクト全体を危うくしかねない。
noteJa.usage: jeopardise + jobs/safety/future の形。英式つづりは -ise。

noteKo.exampleTr: 지불 지연은 프로젝트 전체를 위태롭게 할 수 있다.

job.ex: He found a job in a bank.

jobs.ex: The new factory will create jobs.

keep.en: continue or hold at a level
keep.ex: Keep costs as low as you can.

keeping.ex: Keeping the peace is the army's job.
keeping.zh: 維持（keeping the peace：維持和平）

knowing.ex: He left without knowing the answer.

labour.ex: The country faces a labour shortage.

lamented.ex: Locals lamented the closure of the old shop.

last.en: coming at the end (at the last minute: very late)
last.ex: He packed his bag at the last minute.

leaving.en: going away from a place or job
leaving.ex: After leaving school, he got a job.

likewise.ex: Teachers were thanked, and parents likewise.

made.ex: He made a short speech after dinner.

maintained.ex: She maintained that she had done nothing wrong.

manage.ex: She manages a team of ten people.

management.en: the people who run a company
management.ex: Management agreed to meet the union.

margins.en: the difference between costs and selling price
margins.ex: Shops face thin margins after rent rises.

mere.ex: The film lasts a mere ninety minutes.

million.ex: The city has over one million people.

minister.ex: The health minister visited the hospital.

money.ex: The school needs more money for books.

months.ex: The work will take six months.

more.ex: We need more time to finish.

nevertheless.ex: It was cold; nevertheless, we went out.

new.ex: The city opened a new library.

nominal.ex: They charge a nominal fee for entry.

example.en: Visitors pay a nominal fee to enter the garden.
example.zh: 遊客只需付象徵性的費用就能進入花園。

note.usage: nominal fee / sum / price：象徵性費用；也可指「名義上的」。

noteEn.meaning: very small, not the real value.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los visitantes pagan una tarifa simbólica para entrar.
noteEs.usage: Se usa nominal fee / sum / price.

noteHi.exampleTr: आगंतुक बगीचे में जाने के लिए नाममात्र शुल्क देते हैं।
noteHi.usage: nominal fee / sum आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 訪問者はわずかな料金で庭園に入れる。
noteJa.meaning: 名目上の；ごくわずかな。
noteJa.usage: nominal fee / sum の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 방문객은 정원에 들어가려면 소액의 요금을 낸다.

normal.ex: It looks like a normal pen.

not.ex: The plan is not ready yet.

objective.ex: Our main objective is to cut costs.

on.ex: Voting will go on for nine days.

open.ex: Booking will open on Monday morning.

operates.ex: The machine operates only when the door is closed.

operation.ex: The new system improved the daily operation of the hospital.

options.ex: There are three options for the new road.

order.ex: We left early in order to catch the bus.

others.ex: Some agreed, but others did not.

out.en: used in phrases like work out, spell out
out.ex: Can you spell out your name?
out.hi: हिसाब लगाना (work out); अक्षर-अक्षर बताना (spell out)
out.ko: (work out: ~이 되다; spell out: 철자를 쓰다)

outlets.ex: The brand has 50 outlets across Europe.

outside.en: not from or part of something

over.ex: Over half of the students passed.

owner.en: a person or company that owns something
owner.ex: The owner of the café is very friendly.

owners.en: people or firms that own something
owners.ex: The owners plan to sell the hotel.

parent.en: the company that owns another company
parent.ex: Profits went to the British parent.

parts.ex: Some parts of the film were boring.

party.ex: The party will choose a new leader in spring.

past.ex: In the past, people walked to school.

portfolio.en: a group of things owned together
portfolio.ex: The firm owns a portfolio of hotels.

portion.ex: A portion of the money goes to schools.

position.en: a situation someone or something is in
position.ex: The club is in a difficult position.

pound.en: the money of the United Kingdom
pound.ex: A coffee costs about three pounds in London.

precarious.ex: Many families face a precarious situation.

example.en: Many young workers are in precarious jobs.
example.zh: 許多年輕勞工從事不穩定的工作。

note.usage: 常修飾 position, situation, finances；in a precarious position 很常見。

noteEn.meaning: not safe or steady; likely to get worse.

noteEs.usage: Se usa con position, situation, finances.

noteHi.exampleTr: कई युवा कर्मचारी अस्थिर नौकरियों में हैं।
noteHi.usage: precarious position / finances आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 多くの若い労働者が不安定な仕事に就いている。
noteJa.usage: precarious position / finances などの形で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 많은 젊은 노동자가 불안정한 일자리에 있다.
noteKo.usage: precarious position / finances 형태로 자주 쓴다.

preceding.ex: Sales rose compared with the preceding month.

preserving.en: saving something so it is not lost

pressure.en: strong demand or force from people
pressure.ex: The minister is under pressure to resign.

previous.ex: The previous owner lived here for years.

prices.en: amounts of money paid for things

prior.ex: Please arrive prior to the meeting.

priority.zh: 優先事項（top priority：首要任務）

problems.en: things that are difficult or wrong
problems.ex: The company had money problems for years.

profit.en: money made after costs are paid
profit.ex: The café made a small profit last year.

profound.ex: The internet had a profound effect on work.

prompted.ex: The storm prompted the school to close early.

putting.en: (putting up) building or fixing in place
putting.ex: They are putting up new signs.

recent.ex: The most recent survey shows a change.

reductions.ex: The reductions will hit schools hardest.

retailer.en: a company that sells to the public
retailer.ex: The retailer opened a store in Cork.

retailer's.ex: The retailer's profits fell this year.

retailers.en: shops or companies that sell goods to people
retailers.ex: Many retailers offer discounts in January.

rise.ex: There was a sharp rise in prices.

risk.en: a chance of something bad happening
risk.ex: There is a high risk of flooding.

running.ex: They kept the café running for years.

example.en: New rules will safeguard workers' pensions.
example.zh: 新規定將保障勞工的退休金。

note.usage: 動詞 safeguard + jobs / interests / rights；也可作名詞「保障措施」。

noteEn.meaning: protect something from harm or loss.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las nuevas normas protegerán las pensiones de los trabajadores.
noteEs.usage: Se usa safeguard jobs / interests / rights.

noteHi.exampleTr: नए नियम कर्मचारियों की पेंशन की रक्षा करेंगे।
noteHi.usage: safeguard jobs / rights आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい規則は労働者の年金を守る。
noteJa.usage: safeguard jobs / rights の形が多い。名詞では「保護策」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 규정은 노동자의 연금을 보호할 것이다.
noteKo.usage: safeguard jobs / rights 형태가 흔하다. 명사로는 '안전장치'.

said.ex: She said the bus was late again.

salvage.ex: They tried to salvage the old boat.

example.en: Talks continued late into the night to salvage the deal.
example.zh: 談判持續到深夜，以挽救這筆交易。

note.meaning: 搶救；挽救（快失去的東西）。
note.usage: salvage + something from/out of；常見 salvage the business / a deal / one's reputation。

noteEn.meaning: save something that is in danger of being lost.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las conversaciones siguieron hasta tarde para salvar el acuerdo.
noteEs.meaning: salvar algo que está a punto de perderse.
noteEs.usage: Se usa salvage a deal / the situation.

noteHi.exampleTr: सौदे को बचाने के लिए बातचीत देर रात तक चली।
noteHi.usage: salvage a deal / the situation आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 取引を救うため、協議は深夜まで続いた。
noteJa.meaning: 失われそうなものを救う。
noteJa.usage: salvage a deal / the situation の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 거래를 살리기 위해 협상이 밤늦게까지 이어졌다.
noteKo.usage: salvage a deal / the situation 형태가 흔하다.

save.ex: Volunteers worked hard to save the old theatre.

saved.ex: We saved fifty euro by booking early.

savings.en: money not spent because costs were cut
savings.ex: The new heating gave big savings.

shop.ex: She runs a small shop in the village.

shops.ex: The local shop closes at nine.

similarly.ex: Prices rose, and wages rose similarly.

sinn.en: part of Sinn Féin, an Irish political party

snapped.ex: Fans snapped up all the tickets.

some.en: a number of, but not all

spokesperson.en: a person who speaks for a group
spokesperson.ex: A company spokesperson refused to comment on the story.

squeezed.ex: Families are squeezed by rising rents.

staff.en: the people who work for an organisation

stakeholders.en: people or groups affected by something
stakeholders.ex: The council met all stakeholders before deciding.

example.en: The council will consult stakeholders before deciding.
example.zh: 市議會在決定前會諮詢各利害關係人。

note.meaning: 利害關係人；與某事有利益關係的人或團體。
note.usage: 正式商業或政策用語；consult / engage with stakeholders。

noteEn.meaning: people or groups who are affected by something.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ayuntamiento consultará a las partes interesadas antes de decidir.
noteEs.usage: Término formal: consult / engage with stakeholders.

noteHi.exampleTr: परिषद निर्णय से पहले हितधारकों से परामर्श करेगी।
noteHi.meaning: हितधारक; जिन पर किसी बात का असर पड़ता है।
noteHi.usage: consult / engage with stakeholders औपचारिक प्रयोग है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 議会は決定前に利害関係者に意見を聞く。
noteJa.usage: consult / engage with stakeholders のように使う正式な語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 의회는 결정 전에 이해관계자들과 협의할 것이다.
noteKo.usage: consult / engage with stakeholders 처럼 쓰는 격식어.

stated.ex: The letter stated that he had been fired.

stay.en: continue to be in a place or state
stay.ex: The shops will stay open late.

still.ex: It was cold. Still, we went swimming.

strain.ex: Rent is a big financial strain.

stressed.en: said strongly that it is important
stressed.ex: She stressed the need for care.

strong.ex: We need a strong plan to cut pollution.

struggling.en: finding it hard to do something
struggling.ex: Many families are struggling with high bills.

subsequently.ex: He was subsequently given a new role.

substantial.ex: The town received a substantial grant.

sum.ex: They paid a large sum for the house.

supermarkets.ex: You can buy uniforms in supermarkets now.

susceptible.en: likely to be harmed by something
susceptible.ex: Old people are susceptible to colds.

example.en: Young lambs are highly susceptible to the virus.
example.zh: 小羊非常容易感染這種病毒。

note.usage: 常接 to：susceptible to disease／infection；正式用語，常見於醫學與科學寫作。

noteEn.meaning: easily harmed or infected by something.
noteEn.usage: Often 'susceptible to' + a disease or problem.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los corderos jóvenes son muy susceptibles al virus.

paragraphs: Poundland is a company that runs cheap shops. In Ireland, its shops are called Dealz. Now the company is in serious money trouble.
On Wednesday, the company went into administration. This means outside experts now control it. They will try to save some of the shops.
About 11,000 jobs are at risk in the UK and Ireland. There are about 600 shops. In Ireland, Dealz has about 40 shops and 1,150 workers.
The shops will stay open for now. But workers do not know if they will have a job in January.
Politicians want the Government to help. They asked a government minister, Peter Burke, to talk to the owners quickly.
sentZh: Poundland是一家經營平價商店的公司。
在愛爾蘭，它的店叫做Dealz。
現在這家公司陷入嚴重的財務困境。
週三，公司進入了破產管理程序。
這表示現在由外部專家接管公司。
他們會設法保住部分門市。
英國和愛爾蘭約有1萬1000個工作岌岌可危。
門市大約有600家。
在愛爾蘭，Dealz約有40家店和1150名員工。
目前這些商店會繼續營業。
但員工不知道一月時是否還有工作。
政治人物希望政府出手幫忙。
他們要求政府部長彼得·伯克盡快與業主談話。

paragraphs: Poundland, the discount shop company that trades as Dealz in Ireland, has gone into administration. About 11,000 jobs and 600 shops in the UK and Ireland are now at risk.

In Ireland, Dealz has about 40 shops and employs 1,150 people. Its owner, the American investment company Gordon Brothers, has asked a firm called AlixPartners to manage the business and try to save parts of it.
AlixPartners said the shops will keep trading as normal for now. It said it wants to work with the UK government, trade unions and others to find the best way forward.

The company has had problems for some time. Its last owner, the Polish company Pepco Group, said the business was already weak. A rise in business taxes in the UK made things harder. Gordon Brothers bought it for just one pound.
The owner said staff had saved £100 million in costs over the past year. But high prices and strong competition from supermarkets still hurt the business.

Irish politicians are worried. Ged Nash of the Labour Party said workers are going to work just weeks before Christmas without knowing if they will still have a job in January. He asked Enterprise Minister Peter Burke to contact the owners at once.
Sinn Féin's Johnny Guirke also called on the company and the Government to act quickly to protect jobs.
sentZh: 在愛爾蘭以Dealz名義經營的折扣商店公司Poundland已進入破產管理。
英國和愛爾蘭約1萬1000個工作和600家商店如今面臨風險。
在愛爾蘭，Dealz約有40家店，僱用1150人。
其業主美國投資公司Gordon Brothers已請AlixPartners公司管理業務，並設法挽救部分事業。
AlixPartners表示，商店目前將照常營業。
它說希望與英國政府、工會及其他各方合作，找出最佳的前進方向。
這家公司的問題已存在一段時間。
其前任業主波蘭的Pepco集團表示，這項業務原本就很疲弱。
英國調高營業稅讓情況更加困難。
Gordon Brothers只用一英鎊就買下了它。
業主表示，員工在過去一年節省了1億英鎊的成本。
但高物價和超市的激烈競爭仍然打擊了業務。
愛爾蘭政治人物感到憂心。
工黨的格德·納許說，員工在耶誕節前幾週去上班，卻不知道一月是否還保得住工作。
他要求企業部長彼得·伯克立即聯絡業主。
新芬黨的強尼·吉爾克也呼籲公司和政府迅速採取行動保護工作。

paragraphs: Poundland, the budget retailer that operates as Dealz in Ireland, has entered administration, putting around 11,000 jobs and 600 stores across the UK and Ireland at risk.
The chain employs 1,150 people in about 40 stores in Ireland. Its owner, US investment firm Gordon Brothers, has appointed administrators AlixPartners to try to rescue parts of the business.

AlixPartners said the stores would continue trading as normal while it explores options to keep at least some of the company running. Its priority, it said, is to work with all stakeholders, including the UK government and trade unions.

The retailer has been struggling for some time. Its previous owner, Polish discount group Pepco, said the business was already under pressure before a rise in UK business taxes added further strain. Gordon Brothers acquired it for a symbolic £1, along with more than 800 stores.

According to the owner, management and staff delivered £100 million in cost savings over the past 12 months. However, it warned that the company remained vulnerable to inflation and any fall in sales. Discount chains have faced high inflation and fierce competition from supermarkets in recent years.

The news prompted concern among Irish politicians. Labour's finance spokesperson, Ged Nash, said staff were heading into work weeks before Christmas unsure whether they would have a job in January. He urged Enterprise Minister Peter Burke to contact Gordon Brothers and AlixPartners immediately.
Sinn Féin's workers' rights spokesperson, Johnny Guirke, called on the administrators, the company and the Government to engage urgently to protect jobs and stores.
sentZh: 在愛爾蘭以Dealz名義營運的平價零售商Poundland已進入破產管理，使英國和愛爾蘭約1萬1000個工作和600家門市面臨風險。
該連鎖店在愛爾蘭約40家門市中僱用1150人。
其業主美國投資公司Gordon Brothers已任命AlixPartners為破產管理人，設法挽救部分業務。
AlixPartners表示，在探討讓公司至少部分業務繼續運作的方案期間，門市將照常營業。
它說，首要任務是與所有利害關係人合作，包括英國政府和工會。
這家零售商已苦撐一段時間。
其前任業主波蘭折扣集團Pepco表示，在英國營業稅調漲進一步加重壓力之前，這項業務就已承受壓力。
Gordon Brothers以象徵性的1英鎊收購了它，連同800多家門市。
據業主表示，管理層和員工在過去12個月內節省了1億英鎊的成本。
然而，它警告公司仍容易受到通膨及銷售下滑的影響。
近年來，折扣連鎖店面臨高通膨和來自超市的激烈競爭。
這則消息引起愛爾蘭政治人物的關切。
工黨財政發言人格德·納許表示，員工在耶誕節前幾週上班，卻不確定一月是否還有工作。
他敦促企業部長彼得·伯克立即聯絡Gordon Brothers和AlixPartners。
新芬黨勞工權益發言人強尼·吉爾克呼籲破產管理人、公司和政府緊急協商，以保護工作和門市。

paragraphs: Poundland, the discount retailer that trades under the Dealz banner in Ireland, has collapsed into administration, leaving some 11,000 jobs and 600 outlets across the UK and Ireland hanging in the balance.

In Ireland, the chain operates roughly 40 stores and employs 1,150 staff. Its owner, the American investment house Gordon Brothers, has brought in AlixPartners as administrators in a bid to salvage viable parts of the business.

The administrators stressed that the shops would carry on trading as usual while they weigh up ways of keeping at least a portion of the operation afloat. They pledged to work closely with stakeholders, among them the UK government and trade unions.

The retailer's troubles are far from new. Its former parent, the Polish discounter Pepco Group, had acknowledged that the business was already floundering before an increase in UK business taxes compounded its difficulties. Gordon Brothers snapped it up for a nominal £1, together with a portfolio of more than 800 stores.

The owner maintained that management and employees had wrung £100 million in savings out of the business over the past year, yet conceded that it remained exposed to inflation and to any erosion of sales or margins. Discounters have been squeezed by persistent inflation and cut-throat competition from supermarkets.

The development has alarmed Irish politicians. Labour's finance spokesperson, Ged Nash, lamented that staff were turning up for work mere weeks before Christmas with no certainty of a job in January, and urged Enterprise Minister Peter Burke to contact the owners without delay.
Sinn Féin's Johnny Guirke likewise demanded urgent engagement between the administrators, the company and the Government to safeguard jobs.
sentZh: 在愛爾蘭以Dealz品牌經營的折扣零售商Poundland已倒閉並進入破產管理，使英國和愛爾蘭約1萬1000個工作和600家門市前途未卜。
在愛爾蘭，該連鎖店經營約40家門市，僱用1150名員工。
其業主美國投資公司Gordon Brothers已請來AlixPartners擔任破產管理人，力圖搶救仍可存活的業務。
破產管理人強調，在他們權衡如何讓至少一部分業務撐下去的同時，商店將照常營業。
他們承諾與包括英國政府和工會在內的利害關係人密切合作。
這家零售商的困境絕非新鮮事。
其前母公司波蘭折扣商Pepco集團曾承認，在英國營業稅調漲令困難雪上加霜之前，業務就已陷入掙扎。
Gordon Brothers以象徵性的1英鎊將其買下，連同800多家門市的資產組合。
業主堅稱，管理層和員工在過去一年設法從營運中省下了1億英鎊，但也承認公司仍易受通膨以及銷售或利潤率下滑的衝擊。
折扣商一直受到持續通膨和超市殘酷競爭的雙重擠壓。
這一事態令愛爾蘭政治人物深感憂慮。
工黨財政發言人格德·納許感嘆，員工在耶誕節前短短幾週上班，卻無法確定一月是否還有工作，並敦促企業部長彼得·伯克立刻聯絡業主。
新芬黨的強尼·吉爾克同樣要求破產管理人、公司與政府緊急協商，以保障工作。

paragraphs: Poundland, the discount retailer which operates as Dealz in Ireland, has entered administration, thereby jeopardising approximately 11,000 jobs and 600 stores across the United Kingdom and Ireland.

The Irish arm of the business comprises around 40 stores and 1,150 employees. Its owner, the American investment firm Gordon Brothers, has appointed AlixPartners as administrators with a view to preserving those elements of the company that remain viable.

The administrators have indicated that trading will continue as normal while alternative options are evaluated. They have further stated that their primary objective is to collaborate with all relevant stakeholders, including the UK government and trade unions.

The retailer's difficulties are by no means unprecedented. Its previous owner, Pepco Group, had acknowledged that the business was already in a precarious position prior to an increase in UK business taxation, which consequently intensified the pressure. Gordon Brothers subsequently acquired the company for a nominal sum of £1.

According to the owner, cost reductions amounting to £100 million were achieved over the preceding twelve months. Nevertheless, the company remains highly susceptible to inflation and to any substantial decline in sales or profit margins. Indeed, discount retailers have been adversely affected by sustained inflation and intense competition from supermarkets.

The announcement has generated considerable concern among Irish politicians. Ged Nash, the Labour Party's finance spokesperson, emphasised that employees face profound uncertainty regarding their employment prospects in January, and called upon Enterprise Minister Peter Burke to contact the owners immediately.
Similarly, Sinn Féin's Johnny Guirke urged all parties to engage without delay in order to safeguard jobs.

其前任業主Pepco集團曾承認，在英國營業稅提高之前，業務就已處於岌岌可危的境地，而加稅因此加劇了壓力。

儘管如此，公司仍極易受到通膨以及銷售或利潤率大幅下滑的影響。
